chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hammad from Hariz from Zurara said:
Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: "Determination (of direction) is sufficient always if the direction of the Qibla is not known."

key_terms.التَّحَرِّي: Determination or careful search for the Qibla direction
key_terms.الْقِبْلَةِ: The Qibla, the direction of prayer towards the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is sufficient for prayer if the exact direction of the Qibla is unknown?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Abu Ja'far (al-Baqir) establishes that when the precise direction of the Qibla is unknown, the sincere effort of determination (*al-tahrir*) suffices for the validity of prayer. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-yaqin bi'l-majhul* (certainty amidst uncertainty), relieving the believer from the burden of perfection when knowledge is genuinely lacking. It highlights the balance between strict adherence to ritual direction and divine mercy in cases of genuine ignorance.
